transcript:
--- Meeting Header ---
Date: 2025-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Rashmi Patel (CTO - Meridian Insights), Ethan Kim (Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (ML Eng)

--- Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect) ---
Redwood did an Optimize demo focused on batching and prefix / K V cache economics. We pulled in cost simulations for three scenarios: conservative batching (low latency), aggressive batching (high throughput), and sessionized prefix caching with prefetch. Meridian's main asks: keep p95 < 250ms for chat, reduce per-conversation cost ~30% vs current baseline, and preserve data residency controls.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription may contain errors) ---
[00:00:05] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Laura, AE at Redwood, and with me is Diego, our systems SE. How are you folks doing?
[00:00:12] Rashmi Patel: Doing well, thanks. Busy quarter but excited to talk through the cost bits.
[00:00:18] Diego Martinez: Great. Quick agenda: we'll run a short recap of Redwood Optimize, then jump into a cost sim using your sample traces, and finish with recommended configs for batching and prefix / K-V cache.
[00:00:30] Ethan Kim: Sounds good. We sent over traces last week - ~10k session traces, mostly chat with variable lengths.
[00:00:36] Diego Martinez: Perfect, that's exactly what we used.
[00:00:40] Sofia Alvarez: Quick note — our current setup is self-hosted on k8s with quantized Llama-2 style weights, token-level billing is rough for us right now. We see a lot of short queries and occasional long sessions. Our p99 tails are killing throughput.
[00:00:55] Laura Chen: Thanks. We'll focus on the p95/p99 tail mitigation while showing tradeoffs. One immediate thing: are you comfortable with a small bump in per-request latency if it gives you a 20-40% per-token cost reduction?
[00:01:08] Rashmi Patel: Depends—p95 is non-negotiable for the UI team. If we can keep p95 under 250ms, we can consider small increases to p99 during spikes.
[00:01:18] Diego Martinez: Understood. We'll set the latency budget at 250ms for p95 in the model.
[00:01:24] [00:01:30] Laura Chen: Ok jumping to the simulation — we loaded your trace sample and simulated three configs:
[00:01:36] - Baseline: current concurrency + no KV/prefix caching, commit to same model size.
[00:01:42] - Batch-first: 40ms batching window, bigger batch sizes, active concurrency pooling.
[00:01:48] - Cache-first: sessionization + prefix K V cache with prefetch heuristics for multi-turn flows.
[00:01:55] [00:02:00] Diego Martinez: Note on the transcribe here, sometimes our system refers to K-V as just 'K V' or 'kay vee' in older notes, so you'll see that in the export.
[00:02:08] Ethan Kim: Can you explain the prefetch bit again? We worry about wasted compute if we prefetch wrongly.
[00:02:14] Diego Martinez: Yeah, good point. Prefetch is heuristic-based: for sessions where we detect high-turn probability (bot confirms user intent, long conversation), we precompute a KV set for the next N tokens — usually 64 to 128 tokens — to avoid repeated full attention passes. We model hit-rate vs wasted work in the sim.
[00:02:34] Sofia Alvarez: What's the impact on cold-start? If a session arrives cold, prefetch could increase initial latency.
[00:02:40] Diego Martinez: Right — cold-start hits are the main downside. That's why we recommend tiered TTL and background prefetching only for sessions surpassing a threshold. You can also use a small on-request fast-path (no prefetch) while background prefetch warms the cache.
[00:02:53] [00:03:00] Laura Chen: In the sim results — baseline per-conv cost was our reference. Batch-first with 40ms window saved ~18% on per-token unit cost but increased tail latency; cache-first saved ~34% with careful TTLs and sessionization.
[00:03:16] Rashmi Patel: 34% is compelling. How stable is that in real traffic with spikes?
[00:03:22] Diego Martinez: We ran a spike scenario (2x burst) — cache-first holds up better because session affinity reduces repeated full-decoding work. Batching helps throughput but can add p99 in bursts if queueing grows.
[00:03:35] Ethan Kim: What's the recommended max_batch_size and concurrency for our footprint? We're running A100s with mixed-instance types.
[00:03:42] Diego Martinez: For your token distribution, we'd recommend a max_batch_size of 48 for throughput-critical routes, but set latency-sensitive routes to max_batch_size 12 with a 20-30ms batching window. Also use per-route policies in the console to route low-latency traffic to dedicated small-batch pools.
[00:03:59] Sofia Alvarez: Per-route policies — is that in the hosted API or only on Dedicated?
[00:04:03] Laura Chen: Both; the same API and config semantics apply. For Dedicated we can reserve pools; for hosted you can set policies that route to lower-latency tiers.
[00:04:12] [00:04:20] Rashmi Patel: Security: we need KMS integration and audit logs for all inference calls. Also data residency in eu-west-1 for EU customers. Can Redwood support that for a pilot?
[00:04:28] Laura Chen: Yes. For Private or Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering. We'll include a compliance appendix in the docs.
[00:04:36] Diego Martinez: Quick demo clip — showing the console: here's the Optimize panel where we surface cost delta per change. You can toggle batching window slider and see simulated per-token cost & latency curve.
[00:04:50] [00:05:00] Laura Chen: (screen share) I'm toggling batching from 10ms to 100ms — notice per-token cost drops along the curve but p99 spikes after ~70ms in this traffic shape. This is where the latency budget becomes the guardrail.
[00:05:14] Ethan Kim: Can the console simulate mixed strategies? Like cache-first for chat, batch-first for high-throughput NLP jobs?
[00:05:20] Diego Martinez: Yep — per-route policies let you apply different profiles. We also recommend a fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) if the primary pool is saturated. That preserves availability.
[00:05:32] [00:05:40] Sofia Alvarez: For prefix cache eviction — what eviction policy do you suggest? LRU? TTL-based?
[00:05:44] Diego Martinez: A combination: TTL tuned to session semantics (e.g., 30-120s for interactive chat), plus size-based LRU eviction. For high-turn sessions, prefetch keeps a working set pinned for that session.
[00:05:58] Rashmi Patel: How granular are the cost numbers? We need line items for GPU time, memory, and prefetch overhead.
[00:06:05] Laura Chen: The Optimize simulation outputs breakdowns: raw GPU-seconds, KV cache hits (and estimated compute saved), batching overhead, and average tokens per request. We'll include the CSV export with cost breakout.
[00:06:16] [00:06:30] Diego Martinez: One more nuance — KV cache effectiveness increases for models with long context and where the user repeats system prompts. If you have a lot of re-used prefix content we see hit rates >60%.
[00:06:40] Ethan Kim: Our system inserts an analytics header in each prompt which changes per-turn; does that ruin cache hits?
[00:06:46] Sofia Alvarez: Yes we do that currently for debugging.
[00:06:48] Diego Martinez: Small mutable headers will reduce hit rates. We recommend separating stable prefix (system prompt, persona) from ephemera and send metadata in a separate header so the cache key stays stable.
[00:06:58] [00:07:05] Laura Chen: On pilot design: Diego suggests two parallel benches — a synthetic concurrency bench to validate tail behavior, and a traffic-replay bench using your traces to measure real hit-rate. After that a short live pilot routing 10% of traffic to the cache-first pool.
[00:07:20] Rashmi Patel: Timeline? We need to get internal approvals.
[00:07:23] Laura Chen: We're proposing a 3-week bench (replay + synthetic) + 1-week live pilot. That fits early January start.
[00:07:31] [00:07:40] Ethan Kim: For deployment, will this require code changes server-side? We prefer config-first.
[00:07:45] Diego Martinez: Minimal code changes: you will need to separate prefix content and set a session ID to enable sessionization. The rest is config in the Redwood Console / API. We'll provide a migration guide.
[00:07:58] Sofia Alvarez: What about multi-region failover? If eu-west-1 is saturated, can we route to us-west with a different model and still preserve residency constraints?
[00:08:06] Laura Chen: For EU-only data residency you can restrict fallback to EU regions only. Alternatively, you can allow non-sensitive fallbacks to other regions, but that's a policy decision. We'll include routing examples.
[00:08:18] [00:08:30] Diego Martinez: Ok demo deeper — showing the cost sim CSV. Here we have columns: scenario, p50, p95, p99, per_conv_cost, gpu_seconds, cache_hits. For Meridian's traces: baseline p95=180ms, p99=520ms, per_conv_cost $0.12. Cache-first p95=190ms, p99=320ms, per_conv_cost $0.08. Batch-first p95=155ms, p99=740ms, per_conv_cost $0.098.
[00:08:56] Rashmi Patel: Those p99 differences are significant. Noted.
[00:09:00] [00:09:10] Ethan Kim: During the bench, what metrics should we watch?
[00:09:14] Diego Martinez: Key metrics: cache hit-rate, avg token per request, GPU occupancy, queueing latency, p95/p99, and abort/error rates. We'll instrument tracing hooks and show example dashboards.
[00:09:26] Sofia Alvarez: Any gotchas on batching + KV interaction?
[00:09:29] Diego Martinez: Yes — batching and cache together can create complicated ordering if your cache prefetch modifies request path. We recommend deterministic hashing for session affinity and a short prefetch window that doesn't block the fast-path.
[00:09:44] [00:09:52] Laura Chen: Alright, to recap: recommended pilot config = cache-first for chat routes with sessionization, TTL 60s, prefetch threshold 3-turns, max_batch_size 48 for background workers, and a low-latency pool (batch_size 12, window 20-30ms) for p95-sensitive traffic.
[00:10:10] Rashmi Patel: Sounds reasonable. We'll need the written playbook and the bench scripts.
[00:10:14] Laura Chen: We'll send those after the call. Diego, anything else?
[00:10:18] Diego Martinez: I'll attach a sample bench script and a reduced sample of the CSV outputs so you can review. Also a short doc on cache key hygiene to keep hit-rates high.
[00:10:28] [00:10:35] Ethan Kim: One last question — pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted during pilot?
[00:10:39] Laura Chen: For pilot we'd propose a hosted pilot with Reserved trial credits applied; if you want Dedicated for the pilot we can provide a time-limited Dedicated eval with a small infra deposit. I'll include both pricing lines.
[00:10:50] Rashmi Patel: Great. Let's close with next steps.
[00:10:54] Laura Chen: Next steps are in the action item list, we'll share: pilot config & pricing (Laura), bench scripts & traces cleaned (Diego), and Meridian to confirm infra + sign NDA (Rashmi). We'll target a kickoff first week of Jan.
[00:11:07] [00:11:15] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks all. Good session.
[00:11:18] Laura Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs.
[00:11:22] [END OF RECORDING]
